Eikichi wears a red shirt with a black leather jacket over it, black pants, and black shoes as well. As for his appearance, he is the eldest son of his family and shares height and physique with his younger sister. He doesn't possess great strength, but thanks to his training as a baseball player, he is quite flexible and skilled at throwing things. His eyes are dull green, while his hair is black.

By the end of 1989, he now notes that he is much older than his sister in height due to his training as in Sagako Busters and the fact that his sister was preserved in an onion.
Personality

Eikichi was a teenager searching for new emotions. Previously, he loved to play baseball until he injured his shoulder. The accident left him out of his team and without motivation to live, feeling like a mediocre man who would never amount to anything. Eikichi was somewhat clumsy and constantly tried to follow the fashion or what others are doing at his school. He was also rebellious by trying to smoke and do things to get his mother's attention.

In his first confrontation with a Sagako, he makes the quick decision to save the old people who were under his influence. Here, he also begins to understand how much his sister risked endeavoring to protect him and his family. He decides that it is his turn to step up and fight as well, defeating the Sagako with his baseball bat and onions. Unfortunately, his power is insufficient and the Sagako runs away.

Yuko 10
Yuko never let Eikichi be clouded by his negative thoughts and encouraged him to move on with his life
He always got along with his sister, even when she was better than him in every way. He was never envious of her, but he always put himself down. Despite everything, he still appreciates her very much and appreciates everything that Yuko was always worrying about him, encouraging him to move on. As such, he would not allow anyone to sully his sister's legacy like Sagako Buster, even going so far as to take on a police officer who was insulting his sister's dream.

He was weak in terms of physique and did not have much of a cognitive level. As the Busters mention, he is technically the opposite of his sister in terms of personality. When he discovered that he could also seal the Sagako, he realized that his power was still very weak and needed training. Both Eikichi's physique and intellect took great strides thanks to the Sagako Busters. Little by little, he becomes more and more confident in himself when he discovers that he can be like his sister and be someone useful for once in his life. Which motivates him to continue fighting side by side with the Busters.

Eikichi 37
Eikichi confronts Higashino for insulting his sister's legacy by killing the Sagako
Although he is always willing to help others despite their situation, he also has downtimes where he feels quite depressed and overwhelmed by what is happening around him. After being hit by Higashino in a forest, Eikichi enters a state of negativity for more than a week. Despite the efforts of the Busters, he cannot get out of it. All he needed at that moment was a “We need you” from the girls for him to feel like a part of the group. It doesn't take long for him to realize his mistake in running into a young Saki, who accidentally runs him over with her bike. Saki tells Eikichi to stop thinking others need him and start acting for himself and decide what he wants to do with his life.

Eikichi 66
MJ encourages Eikichi not to get stuck. Also, he has his back covered, so he needs to worry
Eikichi from the beginning was always willing to continue with the Sagako Busters, even if he was not well treated by Tae. The Busters were the place where he was able to embody himself and find the motivation that took him out of his ordinary farm life that he had. Saving his sister was always what he had in mind, ever since he understood what she was doing for the people of Saga and her family in secret. As his Misogi's power increases, he also begins to understand curses and onions, getting to the point of worrying that they are well sealed. Little by little, he begins to look like her sister and to have the same thoughts as her. Now that he understands the Sagako better, he tries to communicate with one of them, even if it seems impossible.

When the last of the Sagako is sealed away by Tae, Yuko is finally freed from her onion and is proud of her older brother. All the struggles and battles of her brother, she had heard and seen from her onion. Even though Saga was saved, he feels that he couldn't save Tae that day. Jofuku, on the other hand, tells him that he should put the past in the past and not blame other people for something that is his problem. He also tells Eikichi that he's got his back covered, so he doesn't have to worry about anything else.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Skillset

Baseball-playing—Since he practiced baseball and aspired to be a professional, he has excellent bat skills, which allows him to hit hard hits or throw objects at high speed to hit his targets. He faces off against a Sagako with nothing more than a baseball bat. His exorcism abilities are performed through tools passed down from his sister, though he slowly begins to harness his supernatural abilities as well.
Unique Abilities

Misogi—Power that he gains by purifying the Sagakos that appear in Saga.
Exorcisms—Like his sister, he possesses the ability to seal curses using onions. According to Jofuku, his Misogi power increases with each training. Only the Hyodo twins have access to this ability, being able to seal the Sagako using special shields made of Onions. Eikichi has to gradually learn how to use this ability when he first joins.
Etymology

The name Eikichi means “flourish, prosperity, honor, glory, splendor” (栄) (ei) and “lucky, good” (吉) (kichi), which can can be translated as “extremely happy”.
Eikichi's surname Hyodo means “soldier, warrior” (兵) (hyo) and “dynamic, motion, change, confusion” (動) (do).
Trivia

Eikichi was also a victim of Saga's curse, which caused his shoulder accident so that he was not a successful baseball player.
Eikichi is revealed to have been classmates with the Death Metal fans since before they became metalheads.
Although Eikichi is somewhat careless, he cares for Yuko Hyodo when she sees the number of bandages that she always wore at school.
Hanako and Anna start calling him “little brother” due to his relationship with Yuko.
Thanks to Hanako, he is now 1.80 and much more flexible thanks to his “Del Height”. This quality only lasted one chapter of the manga.
He has a strong similarity to Sakura Minamoto, not only is he just as clumsy and acts similarly, but they also get depressed in the same way and tend to be very expressive at times

Franchouchou (フランシュシュ, Furanshushu) — formerly known as Death Musume, then Green Face — is an idol group made up of seven legendary zombie girls resurrected by Kotaro Tatsumi.

His goal is to save the Saga Prefecture and revive the trend of local idols in the process, via the Zombie Land Saga Project.


ADVERTISEMENT
Overview


00:00

41:20

Because they can be persecuted when their real identities are exposed, they are presented with their aliases in public. Because they do not all come from the same era and some are unaware of the contemporary, they tend to show a conservative and old-fashioned stance. Tatsumi's original idea is to “support everyone's feelings beyond the ages” as a reason to collect members of different ages together.

Franchouchou logo
Franchouchou group logo
Sakura was the first to awaken her senses; then the others awakened their senses after the first presentation, except Tae Yamada. The group's provisional names were “Death Musume” and “Green Face” respectively for the first two performances, but they decided to change it to “Franchouchou”.

All of them can eat and drink normally like a living human being. But because they are zombies, their bodies have injuries, scratches, and stitches wrapped in bandages that reveal the cause of death of each one, in addition to having red pupils. When their bodies are put under too much pressure, it causes their joints to pop and loosen, causing their eyeballs to open, and limbs, torso, and head to detach from their bodies.

When they appear as normal idols, Kotaro's abilities allow them to take on the appearance of normal people, but as it is make-up, it is easily washed off by water or rain. Also, in their current state, they can survive serious and fatal injuries such as gunshots, lightning or traffic accidents.

The work that Tatsumi offers them always wears them down by rehearsing daily, and two of the seven maintain a relaxed attitude. They practice singing and dancing in a studio located in a Western-style house.
Goal

After being revived, the girls become idols under the pretext of making Saga popular. However, the group's true goal is to defeat the curse of Saga, which also killed the girls when they were about to bring prosperity to Saga. By making Saga have something that cannot be forgotten and cannot die, the curse attempts are ineffective against them, and thus they can be safe on their way to save Saga.

Real Life

The seiyū of the girls (Kaede Hondo, Asami Tano, Risa Taneda, Maki Kawase, Rika Kinugawa and Minami Tanaka) have made various presentations at various anime events in Japan, in which they stand out by wearing the clothes and things used by their alter egos in anime.[1]

Tourism in Saga Prefecture actually saw a surge during the anime's run, with the Abandoned Mansion in real life attracting a thousand visitors in a single day, more than triple the number of staff expectations!

The fact that it came out of nowhere to become one of the best anime of fall 2018 was something that no one expected. The first week since the first Blu-ray went on sale, it sold around 12,500 copies, easily putting it ahead of the other Fall 2018 Blu-ray anime released alongside SSSS.GRIDMAN in second place with roughly, 8000 copies.

The success of the second season positively affects Saga and its economy. It is not only popular among the Saga population and fans, but Saga companies have collaborated with the anime and their products sell out quickly as soon as they are promoted in the anime.

ADVERTISEMENT

Members

Sakura Minamoto (Zombie #1)—The first zombie to wake up among the group of girls. She was confused as to Kotaro's plan, but she has accepted it and is currently following Kotaro in hopes of becoming an idol and finally living her dream in the afterlife.
Saki Nikaido (Zombie #2)—A former member of the girls-only motorcycle gang located in Saga named Dorami. After accepting her death and resurrection, she decides that taking over Japan by becoming a famous idol group is not as bad as it seems. She becomes the leader of the group and with the help of Ai, guides the group toward a new future.
Ai Mizuno (Zombie #3)—The former lead singer of Sakura's favorite pop idol group, Iron Frill. At first, she was against Kotaro's plan, and she wanted nothing to do with him, but since then, she relented and decided that she is now willing to start her career from scratch. After the failure of EFS, Ai is more willing to have her revenge in the same stadium where she died 12 years ago.
Junko Konno (Zombie #4)—Similar to Ai, she was also a pop idol in her time and was against Kotaro's idea of reviving Saga. After her eyes were opened to the reality of her current situation, she finally gives his plan a chance and becomes an essential member of the group when Ai is away.
Yugiri (Zombie #5)—A former courtesan from the 19th century who has been resurrected in modern Japan. She has decided that being confused about everything would not help matters and has simply agreed to go with the flow of the group. In the past, she made a promise to Kiichi Momozaki that she would see the Saga that Kiichi would create.
Lily Hoshikawa (Zombie #6)—Formerly a child prodigy, she got into television for her father's happiness. Unlike Ai and Junko, she is not against Kotaro's idea and happily follows his plans to enjoy her immortal status and that she will never grow old.
Tae Yamada (Zombie #0)—The only legendary girl whose title and cause of death have not been revealed. Despite not having the ability to communicate properly, Kotaro and the others still invite her to her group activities with welcoming arms. In the past, she owned the girls' house and belonged to the Saga Sagako Busters group that fought against Saga's curse.
Allies/Companions

Kotaro Tatsumi—The energetic founder and producer of the group and Sakura's former high school classmate. He is also the one who provides the girls with a place to stay and acts as their escort. Another reason he started the project was to help Sakura live her dream of becoming an idol and making Saga popular by fighting the curse.
Romero—Kotaro's pet zombie poodle and the group's pet. He gets along quite well with the group and is constantly on the lookout for the girls' safety.
Jofuku—The bartender and the one who revived the girls in the first place for Kotaro's plan. He knows that they were killed by the curse and calls the idol plan completely insane. But since he has no more time to save Saga, he reluctantly accepted this way of saving Saga.
Maimai Yuzuriha (Number #7; temporarily)—The temporary eighth member of Franchouchou, who asked to join after Kotaro indirectly knocks her unconscious and takes her to the mansion to revive her. She resigns from the group days later after she realized that she does not belong, and she still has a life ahead of her.
ADVERTISEMENT

Supporters and Rivals

Notable Supporters

Skull and Bull—The first group of fans of the group that since then has attended all their concerts and defends Franchouchou from any danger.
Drive-In Tori President—Can be seen attending their concerts following their successful commercial shoot for his business.
Takeo Go—Like the president of Drive-In Tori, he can be seen attending the group's concerts following the time Lily sings him a song they wrote for him, which gets him back to watching television without any regrets.
Dorami Biker Gang and Korosuke's Female Assassin Gang—The two rival biker gangs have started to become fans of Franchouchou after the biker gang feud with which Saki intervenes to save Maria from risking her life for a bet.
Reiko Amabuki—After Reiko witnesses Saki's intervention with the two biker gangs, she joins them in becoming new additions to Franchouchou's growing fan base.
Little Girl and her Mother—The little girl was the only one who stuck until the end of the girls' guerrilla performance in Episode 3. She and her mother continue to support Franchouchou by attending their concerts from their debut episode onward.
Arata Ookoba—Although at first, he was against Kotaro's plan to use the dead as entertainment, he realized that he was wrong and agreed to help Kotaro to do a benefit concert in Saga but still mistrusts him.
Temporary Supporters

P.R. manager of the Hisanaka Pharmaceutical Company—She was excited to have the girls help advertise her product. She became traumatized and had her memories wiped due to shock from witnessing the actual identities of the idol group.
Notable Rivals

Iron Frill—As of Episode 15, Iron Frill has been classified as Franchouchou's main rival group during their concert at Saga Arena. After the event, both groups are on hand, and it was Iron Frill who assisted in the Ekimae Fudosan concert to help Franchouchou.
Light Oozora—Lily becomes a new rival to Oozora during her performance in the talent show, Japanese Got Performance in Episode 17. At the end of the episode, the two become friends, and Light supports Franchouchou at their revenge concert.
ADVERTISEMENT

Property

Living Space

Kotaro and the girls live in an old, abandoned mansion located outside Karatsu. In the past, this mansion was the headquarters of Saga Sagako Busters to fight Sagako. The mansion is quite spacious and although it is old, it can still be used without problems for their practices. Unfortunately, the house was destroyed by a storm, but in the prologue of the last episode, it is being rebuilt by the people of Saga in gratitude for the help of the girls.

Kotaro van anime
Kotaro's truck is black and has tinted windows
Transport

Their only mode of transportation is Kotaro’s van, which transports the girls to their concerts and helps them bring their props and other equipment. The van is a 5th generation Toyota HiAce Commuter with a low-roof and second facelift model, released in 2014. The taillights, door handles, wheels, headlight location, and back mirror are modeled accurately. Even the curves of the windows were replicated. The light bus versions also have 1-2 seat configurations, as shown in the show.

Legendary Fanbook (32)
Franchouchou Activity Schedule
Merchandise

Their first article of merchandise is revealed to be, according to Lily, “the ugliest T-shirt (she) has ever seen,” as shown in Episode 5. Despite making the girls wear it during the Gatalympics, Kotaro himself does not wear it during his turn in the mud biking round. Their next wave of merchandise is shown in Episode 6, which includes a custom-tailored face towel with a chibified Romero on it. It is also revealed that Kotaro designed and wrote all their merchandise and songs, as he is responsible for their budget.

Among more products shown in the second season, it shows the album “Franchouchou The Best” which was recorded at the end of 2019 in real life, but in the anime, it was recorded at the beginning of 2019. It also showed that there are also keychains of Romero that Ai uses for her work.

ADVERTISEMENT

Trivia

Their first temporary name, Death Musume, literally translates to “Daughters of Death”, whereas their second temporary name, Green Face, refers to the color of their skins without their human make-up.
In Episode 3, Sakura insists on a group name that starts with “Fran-,” then adds Tae's sound effect while sneezing. “Fran” is likely a reference to Frankenstein, as the girls share physical characteristics with the movie's appearance of the iconic monster, especially Junko, who appears to have been stitched again.
Additionally, the “chouchou” part of their group name is pronounced the same as the Japanese onomatopoeia for the kissing sound.
The name is also a play on the Japanese phrase Furanshūshū (腐乱臭衆), meaning “Decomposing Smelly Group.”
Tae's seiyū was credited as “???” During the first two episodes. Kotono Mitsuishi was subsequently credited in Episode 3.
In addition, Kotono is the only one who does not appear during live performances.
Tae, at 29 years, would be the oldest among the girls in terms of their ages of death. In comparison, Lily would be the youngest, at 12 years.
Conversely, Yugiri would be the oldest in terms of the girls’ chronological ages, with Lily still being the youngest, at 19 years.
Franchouchou’s most performed song is “Mezame RETURNER”, with the song currently having four variants, with the first being “Mezame RETURNER (Electric Returner)”, the second being Ai’s solo from Episode 15, the third being “Electric Returner (Type “R”)” from Episode 16 and the fourth being Maimai’s cover from Episode 19.
Both of Franchouchou’s rivals so far all hail from Tokyo.
As of Episode 19, the group has a total of eight members. With Maimai Yuzuriha being their latest, albeit temporary, addition who went by Number 7.
Throughout the series, we are given a few songs that focus on particular characters. Some characters like Saki and Ai get their songs based on the type of music they enjoy the most (Saki favors the punk-rock genre; Ai is part of a J-Pop idol band). However, Lily and Yugiri's own songs have two genres that are more like who they were, rather than their own favorable music genres.
Lily's song is performed in the style of a Broadway-style ballad number (like the song “Tomorrow” from the Annie musical) as it fits who Lily was as a child prodigy actress, working on many hit dramas before she passed away. Naturally, her connections to her work on drama shows and the way she performs as an idol show that her genre of choice is “show-tunes” rather than anything else.
Yugiri's song begins with an intro that matches the traditional folk music of 19th century Japan, which would fit Yugiri, but follows the main genre of her choice: jazz. While Yugiri died shortly before jazz was invented, she particularly prefers this genre as she fits into her original lifestyle of being an adult artist (i.e., an Oiran) and how her human life of her was scandalous. Thus, this song works in tandem with Yugiri's upbeat, dark, and secretive personality.
The members died in the following order: Yugiri (1882) – Junko (1983) – Tae (1989) – Saki (1997) – Sakura (April 2008) – Ai (August 2008) – Lily (2011).

Hanako wears a red dress and a lab coat over it. Her hair is voluminous and pink with a streak of purple. Her eyes are blue. She also wears various accessories such as heart-shaped earrings and welding glasses made of copper.

Her introduction of the Busters to Eikichi is incredibly extravagant and colorful, with “legendary” titles for all of them. She is the friendliest of the Busters towards Eikichi, almost the opposite of Tae's stern demeanor.

She is very cheerful, cutesy, and prefers more of a supporting role for the Busters. She always supports the others and especially Eikichi, whom she considers as her “little brother”. Iron Frill (アイアンフリル, Aian furiru) is an all-female pop group that happens to be Sakura’s favorite. They are present in both the Zombie Land Saga universe and in real life.


ADVERTISEMENT
History


1/2


Founded around 2003, the first known generation held their first concert at Budokan Live in 2007, shortly after releasing their first album “FANTASTIC LOVERS” and behind-the-scenes training for the concert.

Shortly after this event, in mid-2007 they released their second album and the national tour began, one of these places is Arpino in the city of Karatsu, Saga. Sakura attends this first concert and thanks to Ai she decides to be an idol too. On an unknown date, they release the “FANTASTIC IRON” tour DVD, which Sakura would awkwardly throw at Inui's feet in her senior year of high school.

In 2008, they released the third album “MAJESTIC ROAD”, and with this began a new national tour. On August 4, 2008, Ai Mizuno died in Tosu Stadium after being hit by a bolt of lightning that only hit her. Iron Frill goes into hiatus for several months and years later new generations enter. They had a concert in Saga to commemorate Ai on June 22, 2019, presentation at the Saga Arena stadium where the girls from Franchouchou were their opening act.
ADVERTISEMENT

Description

A fictional idol group that Ai Mizuno belonged to during her lifetime. CD sales were the highest in Japan in 2008. According to Tatsumi, Iron Frill continued to reign at the top in the era of idol groups since 2000, and Ai Mizuno was a core member called “The Center of the Group”. The sudden death during Ai's life became a negative publicity effect that affected the group for several years, but its activities have recently resumed. The generations of Iron Frill constantly change and as of 2018, it is celebrating its 15th anniversary.

In the twelfth episode, the scene where Inui (Tatsumi) picks up the CD with Iron frill released by Sakura is drawn as a memory of Tatsumi. And the live in Arpino concert was seen by all the members through the live video in AbemaTV.
News Article on Ai's Death

Legendary Idol Iron Frill Center Mizuno Ai: What comes to mind when you say “Idol”? The answer that anyone would reply to that question with would be “Iron Frill”. Carrying the title of the Nation's Idol along with their name, a tragedy that no one could predict fell upon them. The death of one of the members that was referred to as the “Immovable center”, Mizuno Ai.

Although it was purely an incident, the death of the girl who made being an idol her entire purpose has turned her into a “Legend” among the fans. In regard to Mizuno Ai personally as an idol, she might not have been such a special existence. Looks, vocals, dance, and performance, all of these traits along with her perseverance. She's also naturally good at looking after others…doing the first one as well.

Ai gif 3
Ai Mizuno is struck by lightning
Overcoming the past…In the name of promoting the third album named “Majestic Road” a nationwide tour was held. Closing in on the last live day, on the third day of the Kyushu live tour in Saga, a tragedy struck. The live stage was designed in a way in which a part of the stage extended into the audience to liven things up, and when the song entered its climax, the members jumped out in their performance. One of the girls who stood out on the stage, Mizuno Ai, was struck directly by lightning. The live was canceled immediately, and Mizuno was brought to the hospital, but her burns were severe, and she had no pulse after she arrived at the hospital.

Incidents involving lightning doesn't seem to be that rare, in my humble view, when near high places or buildings or any construction that would serve as a lightning rod, it seemed that it wouldn't be a surprise if lightning struck, but after conducting some research, it turned out that it was indeed really rare for lightning incidents to happen. There are roughly 20 lightning incidents per year and most of them occur in open ground areas, and among them, 70% of the incidents result in death. It is important to note any high constructs near the area that are made of metal, but considering the circumstances of her death, it wouldn't have been strange for nearby audiences to have been struck as well. But even then, she was the only casualty. A rumor spread among the fans that it was she who protected the fans and took the lightning all by herself. It would be impossible to know the truth, as it is inappropriate to probe further into the minds of the deceased.

Xu Fu, or Jofuku[1] (徐福, Jofuku) is the immortal bartender of the “New Jofuku” bar. He is also the surrogate father of Kiichi Momozaki and Tae Yamada, and the mentor of Kotaro Tatsumi.

His character is based on the alchemist of the same name who served the emperor during the Qin Dynasty, who was sent to find the Elixir of Immortality.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


1/2


Meiji Era

In the Meiji Era, his power was reduced, and he seemed much older than usual, so he was bald and only wore a white robe and a staff to support himself because his back was weak. His voice was muffled and he could barely move. His body was so weak that he had to resort to medication to feel better.

1989

Because Saga was booming, his appearance is much younger than what is seen in the anime. He wears his Bartender outfit, but his body is much stockier and shows muscle. His hair is blonde and partly long. Due to the high presence in the Sagako area and the damage caused by them, he begins to age rapidly over the course of a single day, aging 10 years at a time.

Present

By 1994, he had recovered from the relapse he had in 1989, having the appearance with which he is seen today. He currently works at the Bar New Jofuku in the center of Saga City. He wears a waiter type suit and his hair is completely gray and has a mane that reaches below his neck. He is also partially bald.

ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

Meiji Era

During the Meiji Era, his power was greatly reduced by the non-existence of Saga on the map, so he hysterically searched for a young man who would help him. This young man is Kiichi and with the advice of his grandfather, he tries to return Saga to the place where it was before. During his appearance in Episode 21, he is seen as a grumpy old man who appears to be crazy by shouting that he himself is Saga.

His attitude with Yugiri is very different from the cold man he is with Kotaro, this because Yugiri was taking care of him when he was weak and took care of Kiichi, so he could create his new Saga, so he is quite kind to her. He still has trouble remembering the name of the group. As implied in the first season, Yugiri's favor towards him was because, thanks to her, he can still live because she indirectly restored Saga.

1989

In Gaiden's manga, his personality is further explored with his adoptive daughter, Tae, and whom he welcomed as Saga's savior in this generation to save Saga from Sagako. He likes that Tae calls him father because he feels that Tae is his daughter deep down. He is overprotective according to Tae's perspective, and that's why the two of them distanced themselves for a while and only talked on TV. Jofuku was the boss of the Karatsu Burgers chain where Tae works and is the one who helps her with the purchases to maintain the business.

With the Sagako Busters, he is the mysterious man who tells them how their plans to save Saga are going and manifests himself through the television, vaguely telling them parts of the plan that they must carry out. After a brief reconciliation with Tae, MJ and the Busters decide to work together again to seal the Sagakos that appear in Saga.

Jofuku is later weakened by Sagako, and the destruction of the mansion where they lived causes them to go to the Hyodo house. Jofuku, old and weak, is unable to help the group on their latest mission.

By 1994, he has rejuvenated enough to be stable and opens a new bar in the center of Saga. Although Tae is dead, he tells Eikichi that her soul will continue to protect Saga.

Present

Jofuku 11
Jofuku about to engage in conversation with Yugiri
From what little we know of him, he is a mature man who is not afraid to talk to people and is direct with his conversations, although he likes to play a little cryptic with them as well. During his appearances during the series, he is direct with Kotaro calling his plan crazy, but worried that Yugiri is okay. In episode 13 and the first of the second season, this attitude goes a bit further by insulting Kotaro for his homeless appearance and deliberately confusing Franchouchou's name with “Saga ettes” in reference to the stadium where they failed. This to intentionally provoke Kotaro by telling him to inform the girls that it's over for them so that he comes out of his depression and goes directly to save the group.

Although he is somewhat cold towards Kotaro, he understands his situation and decided to help him with his zombie idol project to save Saga from The Curse of SAGA, though even he admits that the plan is totally crazy. Jofuku and Kotaro seem to have a fairly mature friendship, and he occasionally jokes about the group's name to get attention.

ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Skillset

Bartending—He currently works at a bar and is supposed to have bartending skills.
Natural Abilities

Wide Intellect—With more than 2,200 years of life, Jofuku has accumulated great knowledge of Saga and the entire world, making him a good source of information.
Unique Abilities

Immortality—Because he found the Elixir of Immortality, Jofuku is now fully immortal, but this very immortality is tied to the Saga itself. When Saga is affected by the curse he becomes older and sicker, and when Saga is prosperous, he is younger and stronger.
Rejuvenation and aging—This seems to be a side effect of the elixir; since it is linked to Saga's level of prosperity and collective memory, the powers wax and wane depending on the state of the prefecture.
Necromancy—As mentioned in Episode 20, he can raise the dead, depending on the state of Saga Prefecture. When Saga disappeared from the map, consequently, he lost his powers and his ability to be immortal.
Omnipresence (Limited)—Jofuku can see and sense Saga, as shown when Ito killed several Saga rebels and felt the retaliation for this by losing his power and falling unconscious.
Clairvoyance—Jofuku can moderately see the future and predict certain events that will happen in the future of Saga. However, this power is limited to saying things vaguely or only saying a specific time, so he can't say exact things.
Technology Manipulation—Jofuku can communicate through a television and be aware of the surrounding environment in some unknown way. Probably something to do with his magic that allows him to transmit a figure of himself through a hologram.
Sagako Detection—Jofuku can sense when a Sagako manifests in Saga and guides the Busters towards the direction it appears. But this ability “sucks” according to Eikichi and Anna, not being able to give the exact location where Sagako came from.
Saga Prosperity—Thanks to Saga's prosperity, certain areas of Saga have the power to seal curses due to the love these lands received.
Weaknesses

Saga Curse—Saga's curse continually tries to stop those who are destined to save Saga, so it will prevent it from happening in any way and try to wipe Saga off the map. As Jofuku's power comes from Saga, each altercation against the prefecture constantly weakens him.
ADVERTISEMENT
Trivia

Saga and he are one in body and soul. Therefore, he is Saga. [2]
His character is based on Qin Shi Huang's court magician himself, Xu Fu. Who was ordered by his boss to search for an “elixir of the immortals” on top of the mythical Mount Penglai.[3] He supposedly found the elixir whose name is “Furofuki” on top of Mount Kinryu after arriving in Saga and meeting the locals, indicating that the island he was looking for is actually Saga Prefecture. [4] The elixir was given by a leading wizard of the 8 immortals, Anqi Sheng. This place is known in Chinese mythology as the place where the fruits that give immortality and are capable of reviving the dead grow, strongly indicating that this is the reason the girls were revived.
The bartender is Xu Fu or Jofuku himself, who forced immortality by becoming Saga's kami. Therefore, he says that he is Saga, and his power, appearance, and intellect decreased with Saga's removal from the map. If Yugiri helped restore Saga's name, then she saved him, and it would explain why she owes him so much.
Fukagawa, the mangaka who writes Gaiden, said that Episode 9 has a connection to Zombie Land Saga Gaiden.[5] His affiliation with Yugiri is later confirmed in episode 20.
The footage released at the bar foreshadowed that the association is quite intentional in this Universe, and as confirmed in the credits of Episode 20, it is about Xu Fu himself. Both images in the background of the bar belong to the Jofuku Longevity Hall, the museum and park dedicated to the legends of Xu-Fu in Saga City.
In the first season and the first episode of Revenge, his name was only marked as “Master”, however that changed in Episodes 20 and 21, where speculations about his identity were confirmed when the credits officially called him “Jofuku”.
The “Genkai Zombie Energy Park Project” which he purposely confuses with the Zombie Land Saga Project as in the thirteenth episode is a reference to the Genkai Energy Park, which is a kind of park in Saga that is located next to the power plant containing such exhibits and the like.
Jofuku has the power of divination, as he predicted that Saga would lose its name. He also correctly predicted that some orphan he took in would eventually save Saga. Therefore, it is very likely that he chooses all the girls through divination and resurrects them. Reinforcing the Bagua Theory.
It is revealed that he kept the group photo with Kiichi, Ito, and Yugiri on one of the shelves in his bar, as shown in “The SAGA Incident: Part Two”.
He is the head of the Saga Sagako Busters and the one who told them that the end of Saga will mark the end of the world, so they must stop Sagako before they destroy Saga.
In his own words, the outbreak of Sagakos in Saga marks the beginning of the end of the world in 1999, 10 years after where the manga takes place. Currently, more details of this are unknown.
In Gaiden Chapter 4, we get to see Jofuku at his strongest and healthiest during an economic boom in Saga in the late 1980s

Personality

He was a detective with malice inside. When he caught Anna stealing, he used her and her thieving skills to ambush future robberies that would take place in Tokyo. Everything was going well until a big incident that resulted in Anna escaping. His inability to track down and capture Anna after the Tokyo incident caused him to be demoted until he finally ended up in the middle of nowhere, in Saga. When he finally meets Anna again years later, he asks her for some answers and what she's doing with her life today, since she's still a fugitive. He seems unafraid of getting his hands dirty to serve “his justice” by brutally beating Eikichi when he gets in his way and insulting the Busters' work, belittling them for all they've done.

Keiji 19

Although his first encounter with Sagako ends up scaring him, he showed that he was not afraid to follow one and shoot him 5 times with his gun until he finally died. Knowing the potential that these creatures could bring to the human world, he quickly realizes that Sagakos appear in areas with very high prosperity, and therefore hunts them down. Unlike the Busters, whose goal is to purify them, Higashino seeks to use his abilities to sell them in the human industry.

Keiji 27
Keiji gets angry with Magatsuhi
He shows curiosity about the supernatural events in Saga, first calling them “unknown fauna”. Given the amount of supernatural things that happen around him, he realizes that he is dealing with unknown entities, and he will seek to know the truth behind these beings. Higashino makes a deal with Magatsuhi, a deal with which he will have to eliminate all of Saga's Sagakos so that Magatsuhi can recover her power and fulfill his wish. This shows the more selfish side of him by being driven by his own desires.

When Magatsuhi shows disinterest in fulfilling his promise, he becomes angry with the curse and threatens her, desperately asking for his wish for power. Before firing his gun at Magatsuhi, he is brutally killed by being impaled on one of Magatsuhi's limbs.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Natural Abilities

Investigation—Born from his profession as a police detective, Higashino, when showing curiosity about something, lets it get the best of him and will not rest until he knows the truth behind his concern.
Etymology

Detective in Japanese kanji and in word is entirely different. The difference is that the word (刑事, Keiji) refers to a detective who belongs to the police. While the word (探偵, Tantei) is a detective who does not belong to the police, but before called as a private detective or private investigator.
Trivia

He was assassinated by the same Sagako, responsible for the death of Tae Yamada's parents.
His flashbacks before he died show that he suffered a lot of bullying from his classmates, who treated him as weird and weak, which led to Higashino resenting his classmates and wanting to eliminate those who got in his way.
Higashino's idea of using the Sagako in the industry could have many negative repercussions. Not only would it be altering the curse, but by killing a Sagako without purifying it, it only makes them more powerful.
His conversation with Magatsuhi about removing all of Saga's curses for a “reward” points out that while he has a good intention to remove Sagako, he does so based on his own ego.

Kiichi Momozaki (百崎 喜一, Momozaki Kiichi) was the adoptive son of Jofuku and the former best friend of Shojiro Ito. He was a supporting character who made his debut in “Episode 20”.

He dreams of restoring Saga as a suitable prefecture after it was forcibly merged with neighboring Nagasaki after the Saga Rebellion of 1874.

Personality

Kiichi is a young man with enough energy and a noble heart who wants to regain Saga's glory after the war eight years prior. His father died during the war, so Jofuku took him in as a grandson while also constantly taking care of him.

In fact, it is thanks to Jofuku that Kiichi decides to go out into the streets of Saga to distribute pamphlets to recover Saga's former glory. Whether he is pushed in the streets or his friends take advantage of him, nothing seems to go well for him.

When he meets Yugiri, he instantly falls in love and treats her like a lady, to the point of giving her a comb that she would later use when she was revived. According to Ito's words, they would both form a good couple because they seem to be made for each other.

He is a rather idealistic and childish young man who is willing to fulfill his dreams. Unfortunately, he is ignored by people and everyone around him seems indifferent or opposes his efforts to restore Saga, to the point of getting into trouble with the forces of order.

When he finally gets support for his cause to bring Saga back, he is left aside by his companions who want to go to war to recover Saga, but they are killed by Ito, who was there to stop any rebellion. Because of this, Kiichi feels useless because real people died because of him and his childhood dream.

Yugiri manages to console him and tells Kiichi that these people will not die in vain and that his dream must be fulfilled, no matter how childish it may be. Words that motivate Kiichi to escape Saga and guide his future to make a new Saga.

ADVERTISEMENT

She manifests as a human girl, but with a mask of different entities from Japanese folklore on her head with shaggy, disheveled hair. She wears a white robe and has nothing else to wear. Behind her multiple masks, she takes the appearance of a human girl with white hair.

With this form, she can use the powers of her Sagako and use the spider's limbs to immobilize or damage her opponents.

As Sagako

Magatsuhi heart
Magatsuhi's final form
This Sagako was created from the Spider Egg Sagako seen in the previous chapters of the manga. Her physical appearance is inspired by a large tarantula, reaching at least 10 meters in height and 20 in length. Her limbs are quite long compared to her body, and this allows her to move quickly as well as use them as a weapon. Unlike a normal spider, this Sagako has a round head with multiple eyes and two fangs in front. In her final second stage, her eyes cover her entire body. Magatsuhi's mask can manifest on top of the Sagako's head.

Her final form, after she was defeated with her spider form, is a giant Sagako heart-shaped like her body and torso, with multiple limbs sticking out of the main body. Her eyes are empty and white, while her mouth looks torn, and she has a sinister smile. In the middle of the heart is Magatsuhi, surrounded and held by what appears to be multiple human forms.

ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

She appears grimly in front of Higashino after he throws Doro-chan across the Saga border, vaguely explaining how Sagako works. Despite not being her intention, she makes a deal with Higashino whereby he would get a wish he wanted if he killed the Sagakos so that she could finally regain her power. Her attitude is quite frivolous, and she doesn't talk much with people, reaching the point of not caring about the lives of some humans. When the detective stands in front of her to fulfill his wish, Magatsuhi speaks telepathically with Keiji, and whatever she told him, Keiji didn't take it very well and threatened Magatsuhi to shoot her. When she no longer needs him, she ends up killing him.

After disappearing again, she starts kidnapping women between the ages of 20 and 40 in Saga. Unlike what she was going through with Higashino, she seems to be concerned about their feelings and physical state, putting them in a sleepy state while she had them captured. However, she doesn't seem to mind separating them from their families and keeping them confined from their freedom. Her motivations; seek maternal love and be loved by a family.

Tae death
Tae merges with Magatsuhi
Regardless, it's a curse based on a human girl, so it behaves like one. Her objective was to search for her mother, this being the reason for the kidnappings. Although she tries to finish off Eikichi and Tae when they enter her park, Eikichi tries to communicate with her in her Sagako form, getting an unintelligible response. In one last attempt, he shows her an onion, confusing her and causing her to freak out.

Tae, who seeing that they are losing the battle, sacrifices herself by receiving the Misogi power from Yuko and Eikichi, climbing to the top of the Sagako. There, Tae discovers that Magatsuhi's goal was to seek motherly love and be loved, to never feel alone again. Just like Tae always wanted with her parents. Finally understanding the curse, Tae sacrifices herself, forgiving herself and accepting Magatsuhi to seal the curse within her own body.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Natural Abilities

Sagako Form
Agility—Her body shape and long limbs allow her to maneuver around obstacles with ease and run quite fast.
Limbs as a weapon—Her limbs are quite dangerous, one of the main dangers of this Sagako being to use them to easily kill whoever gets in her way.
Electric powers—Like the girls from Franchouchou, this Sagako would have received electrical powers at the time of the fusion, but was later discharged.
Telepathy—Through telepathy, Magatsuhi can communicate with her targets at a distance.
Human Form
Limb Manifestation—Magatsuhi's human form can change if she is under attack, being able to transform parts of her body into dark limbs that allow her to defend and attack.
Spectral apparition—She briefly appears in front of Higashino to momentarily speak to him, only to disappear moments later.
Unique Abilities

Curse of Saga—She is the first Sagako to appear in Saga. The Sagako, although they are beings of the curse, would be taking away her energy by manifesting in Saga continuously, so she entrusts Keiji to kill them so that she can recover her power. After manifesting as a spider, Sagako's manifestations disappear because she now has all the energy that allowed them to manifest. She also seems to use Saga's prosperous places to gain power.
Weaknesses

Hyodo Farm Onions—As she is also a being of the curse, she is susceptible to the sealing with the onions and their power. In fact, it was thanks to the power that was transmitted to Tae by Eikichi and Yuko, that she was sealed inside Tae's body.
ADVERTISEMENT
Etymology

Magatsuhi-no-kami (Japanese for “kami of the force of misfortune” or “God of calamities”). In Shintoism, divine beings that cause sin, pollution, disaster, and evil. Related terms are Ōmagatsuhi-no-kami, meaning “Great Magatsuhi Kami” and “Yaso-magatsuhi-no-kami”, meaning “Countless Magatsuhi Kami”. [1]
Trivia

This is the first Sagako that we see born from its early stage, this being a child raised by Tae's parents.
Like every curse in Saga, her goal was to target those who brought prosperity to the prefecture. Basically, implying that if Tae's parents spent more time with her daughter, they would bring prosperity.
Likewise, curses only take the form of problems underlying the area of appearance, in this case, Magatsuhi takes the form of a human girl as a reflection of Tae Yamada's parents' abandonment of their daughter.
As such, Magatsuhi's goal in the final arc of the manga was to search for the maternal love that disappeared when she killed Tae's parents in her Sagako form. To fill that void, she began kidnapping women in Saga as a replacement for her mother.
The masks that Magatsuhi wears refer to entities from Japanese mythology.
A Demon Hannya mask is the first. The Hannya are female demons who were consumed by their high level of jealousy. According to legend, her origin was with a jilted young woman whose jealousy turned into rage and anger when she saw that the person she loved, a cleric, was not interested in her. It was because of that inside her, she began to harbor evil, becoming a demon, more specifically, a Hannya.
Magatsuhi's first appearance is with this mask, which would reflect Tae's anger and rage at the abandonment of her parents for their investigation.
The Fox or Kitsune mask is the second. The Kitsune or foxes are an animal that constitutes an element of singular importance in Japanese folklore, to the point where the word is traditionally used to name that spirit of the forest in the form of a fox, whose classic function is to protect forests and villages. According to Japanese mythology, the fox is an intelligent being that has magical abilities, which are increased with age and the acquisition of knowledge.
The first emotion born in Tae's heart as a zombie was familial love for Sakura Minamoto, wherein she sees her as a mother figure. This was not referenced again upon until the very last chapter of the spin-off manga, where both Magatsuhi and Tae come to an agreement and willingly fused with each other over their craving for maternal affection.

Maimai wears a typical school uniform which is green, more specifically she wears a dark blue skirt that reaches up to the knees, a green jacket, and a collared shirt with a pink tie. She also wears glasses that are constantly breaking. Her hair is brown and short, but has a voluminous appearance. Maimai sports a very voluptuous figure, that overall beats even Yugiri's. During her brief stint as a member of Franchouchou, she is assigned the color green.
Personality

Maimai's personality closely resembles Sakura's and has many parallels to her, as seen in the episode. She is cheerful and extremely clumsy and quite impulsive. But once she overcomes those defects, she can act at the same level as her idols, Franchouchou. She never gives up and moves on. After joining Franchouchou she realizes that she doesn't belong there, since Franchouchou is only made up of girls who have had their lives taken and want to move on. So, upon realizing this, she decides to leave the group during her first performance as a member. Maimai's maturity is denoted by not being scared by zombie girls and by keeping their secret by not telling anyone, so she is someone the Franchouchou girls can trust.

She acts like one for Sakura. They are both clumsy, but enthusiastic and determined to succeed, and Maimai admires Sakura and Franchouchou in the same way that Sakura once looked at Ai and Iron Frill. The difference, of course, is that Maimai is still alive; her motivation is simply to live her life to the fullest, while Sakura's (and the other zombies) motivation is to make up for the fact that their lives were shortened, and they never could develop their potential.

Despite spending several hours practicing without doing the correct routine, Maimai refuses to finish the day, an attitude that endears herself to Ai.

During Maimai's stay as a temporary member of Franchouchou, she sports the most curvaceous build out of the girls. Beating Sakura, Tae Yamada, and even Yugiri in terms of body type.
The idea that a fan of Franchouchou discovers their identity as zombies had been raised since the first season, so it was decided to take up that idea and develop the character of Maimai around it. During the first episodes, she was added as an Easter Egg to give the feeling that she was always there.
Her first visible appearance is during the fight at Geils Live House in “episode 13” as a girl in the background. But as she comments in her debut episode, she has been following Franchouchou since their concert in Arpino.

Maria Amabuki (天吹 万梨阿, Amabuki Maria) is the former leader of the now disbanded Dorami Biker Gang, now rebranded as the Dorami Dance Team, which she is the current leader of. She is a supporting character who made her debut in “Episode 9”.

She is the daughter of Reiko Amabuki, whom she was once rebellious towards, as she thought the latter was nothing but a spineless wimp for leaving the gang in favor of becoming a housewife.

Appearance

Casual

Maria is a high school girl with long, wavy light-brown hair that reaches to her waist. It is often tied into two loose space buns, with a single strand dangling down from each of them. She has blunt bangs that frame her face and display her eyes, which are a reddish chestnut color.

She usually wears a Dorami uniform, which is the standard Dorami uniform, consisting of a long red coat with her name and position written on the back in Kanji characters. Underneath, she wears a gray blouse, a black tie, and a long black skirt.

Grocery Store Uniform

Maria is wearing a white shirt and black pants, she has a red apron on the front.

Personality

Maria has a very rebellious and aggressive personality that she developed by hating her, the soft and unnecessarily apologetic attitude of her mother, Reiko Amabuki. She has proclaimed herself the leader of the Dorami motorcycle group, of which she has learned that her mother had been the leader.

She and her gang do this to look threatening to Sakura Minamoto and Lily Hoshikawa, but all they do is make them look silly. She tries to be a tough-talking motorcyclist like her mother in the past, but she is quite inept and very insane for doing it.

This demonstrates a brave but also very reckless side of her. An example is when she confronts the leader of a rival gang, Misa Higashitsuru despite being obviously outmatched and accepting Misa's challenge in a game of chicken. Saki Nikaido lectured Maria in both situations for this recklessness, most likely stemming from her own experience.

After Saki's confrontation, Maria understands that there are other ways to rebel and decides to form the new group “Dorami Dance Team” with her two friends. Besides being much more worried about herself and not scaring her mother by doing crazy things like before. She is even quite nice to Tae Yamada and tries to help her as a friend that is hers.

Policeman A (警察官A, Keisatsukan A) is an unnamed police officer and a major recurring character in Zombie Land Saga.

Although he is more of a threat to zombies than he realizes they are to him, his reasons for repeatedly trying to kill them on sight are perfectly understandable, as he is just an ordinary, generally affable, scared cop.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


00:00

41:20

He is an average adult man who is always seen wearing a Japanese police uniform consisting of a white collared shirt and dark blue shoulder pads and dark blue pants. He carries an S&W Model 37 .38 caliber “Air weight” snub-nosed revolver.
Personality

When first introduced, he has a pretty casual and somewhat cheeky personality. However, he has proven to be extremely fearful and impulsive, as he instantly shot Sakura upon seeing her zombie form even though she initially called for help, and immediately attempts to shoot her again along with Ai and Junko after seeing their zombie appearances.

He seems to think he's a big shot when it comes to getting women, and occasionally tries to flirt with them. Not only do all the girls he interacts with not react to him beyond her police work, but Sakura is also afraid to get close to him, as he reacts badly to her without makeup. In Revenge, he unsuccessfully tries to get close to Junko when she's down for Ai, though to be fair, he starts backing off when he starts to think she's underage.

When he meets Sakura again in Episode 3 in her human form, he seems to recognize her, but can't remember where. Little does he know that she was the zombie he tried to shoot twice. After the events of the third episode, he is relegated to comedy roles and does not directly face the zombie aspect of the show until episode 11. Whenever he sees one of the zombies, he immediately goes crazy with terror and tries to shoot without good aim, although all zombies show sensitivity and have shown no signs of hurting him.

He shoots Sakura out of fear of being a zombie, despite Sakura showing human intelligence and speech, and is then knocked out from behind her. When confronted by a motorcycle rally, despite not comically threatening them, they still scatter as he killed the mood. Again later; he braves the storm-hit flooded areas of Saga, searching for people who may be in trouble. This allows him to save Kotaro and Jofuku from the flooded bar, in which they were trapped for three days.

Romero (ロメロ, Romero) is the undead pet poodle of Kotaro Tatsumi and the mascot for Franchouchou. He is also the first zombie to be successfully resurrected, the first to gain consciousness, and the only known zombified animal.

He is later revealed to once belong to the Momozaki Family in “Episode 20” before being given to Kotaro at some point, thus also becoming the animal companion of the group of girls.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


1/2


Regular Form

Romero is a zombie dog with stitches and bandages over its body, it has different fur in two shades of blue, as well as what appears to be a bruise on the side of his right arm. He has a doll-like right eye and has long blood-stained fangs sticking out of its mouth.

Monstrous Form

In his monstrous form, Romero grows larger and appears more detailed. His only eye is shown to stick out of the socket, and the Saga-shaped scar on the right side of his body is more visible. In his monstrous form he can scare away unwanted passersby effortlessly, and whenever he is with one of the girls it is to prevent people from discovering that they are zombies.

Personality

He is Jofuku's zombie poodle and has accompanied him since ancient times, showing attachment to him when he shows signs of weakness. He was handed over to Kotaro Tatsumi as part of the Zombie Land Saga Project to be a fundamental part of Franchouchou and watch the girls closely, as he is also a zombie.

Due to Romero's zombie appearance, he appears to look and act aggressively, but actually behaves like a normal dog. As he spends more time with Franchouchou, he becomes attached to them. He is very loyal to both Kotaro and the girls.

Like Tae, he generally tries to eat things that aren't even meant to be edible. In Episode 5 he swallows a baseball whole, and in Episode 10 it is implied that he ate a grasshopper that was unlucky enough to get close to him.

He has also proven to be friendly with Sakura; joining her on her morning jog and becoming fiercely protective of her after he is hit by a truck of hers in Episode 10.

Tae and Romero show some form of friendship, the first being a human zombie and the second a zombie dog. They spend an entire episode of Revenge running errands and interacting with the locals together.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Natural Abilities

Enhanced Senses—As a dog, Romero has better senses compared to humans.
Immortality—Similar to the girls, Romero is given the ability to not physically age and stay the same appearance as the age he died, as well as immunity to circumstances that could normally be fatal to humans and animals.
Detachable Limbs—Parts of Romero's body are detachable and can easily be reattached.
Phosphorescent Vision—Although Romero has not shown this feat yet, it is assumed that his eye can also glow in the dark.
Wide Intellect—Romero is shown to be smarter than the average dog.
Skillset

Fishing—As shown in “Episode 10”, Romero can swiftly hunt for aquatic life in his savage form.
Unique Abilities

Monstrous Form—A feat Romero and Tae Yamada shares, they can both morph into scarier versions of themselves that highlights their aggressiveness.
ADVERTISEMENT
Etymology

The surname Romero is a Spanish and Italian surname meaning: A person on a religious journey or pilgrimage from Rome (possibly to Jerusalem); procession of elevated holy items.
Romero is likely a reference to George A. Romero, a film director who is well known for the cult classic zombie movie called Night of the Living Dead.
Trivia

Zombieland Saga 2nd Fanbook 075
Concept art of how zombies are made. Starting out as an amorphous mass that then takes the form of Romero
Romeo's first drawings came out like this and ended up leaving the design as it is. He was pulled purely from instinct, though they weren't sure if that “instinct” was good or not. It goes along with the zombie-like Franchouchou, but it was conceived at a time when they weren't really sure what kind of image they would go with. Stories from everyday life are difficult anyway, so they followed the current form. They added the Sakura ribbon and all that to give it some distinction during the time when the other characters were zombies.
Romero died one month after his third birthday.
Additionally, he shares his date of death with Junko Konno.
Like the girls, it is also unknown how Romero got resurrected.
The only times wherein Romero does not make an appearance (excluding the previous episode recap, next episode preview and outro) is in the fourth, seventh and seventeenth episodes.
Technically speaking, Romero is the first to wake up among the eight zombies Kotaro Tatsumi has resurrected. With Tae only being the first in terms of the zombie humans he has resurrected, and Sakura Minamoto being the first zombified human to gain consciousness.
He is also the first zombified creature and only (conscious) zombified animal among the eight.
Both Romero and the floor of the basement of the Franchouchou Mansion share markings that resemble the Saga Prefecture on them. The basement floor of the mansion has a stain in the shape of the prefecture, whereas Romero's is his bruise.
In “Episode 20”, it is revealed that Romero was once the pet dog of the Momozaki Family during the late 1800s. And that, at the time, he was already living as a zombie.
Despite being also being a zombie, Romero does not seem to need to hide the fact that he is undead. Whenever he joins Kotaro and the girls in public, as he can be seen without his head during the shooting for The Drive-In Tori commercial in the fifth episode.
Romero also makes an appearance in the Zombie Land Saga manga Gaiden: The First Zombie, though only as a background character.

The Saga Sagako Busters (佐賀サガコバスターズ, Saga Sagako Basutāzu) are a group of Sagako hunters who dedicated themselves to fighting curses in Saga.

They were first introduced in the spin-off manga, Zombie Land Saga Gaiden: The First Zombie.


ADVERTISEMENT
Overview


00:00

41:20

They call themselves pure, beautiful and righteous. They fought against the curse that plagued Saga in the late 80s.

Ten years before the events of the Gaiden manga, in 1979, the Sagako Busters group is founded by Jofuku. Thanks to MJ, Tae was able to form a team that is willing to give their lives for the good and prosperity of Saga.

Without Yuko's power, the team would not be able to seal the Sagakos that appear in Saga, so she was an essential piece of the team. Thanks to the “love” the land received from years of cultivation, it made the onions at Hyodo farm special, and the Hyodo twins were given the power to seal curses with these onions. During this time, Hanako Hakase also joins.

After the founding of the group, many applicants for that job joined, including an occultist, a self-proclaimed fortune-teller, and a medium. None of which lasted for more than 3 days within the group. One day, a mysterious girl named Anna Shuri arrives willing to help them despite how crazy it sounds to fight against supernatural beings. In addition to adapting to Hanako's inventions, she is also excellent at battle and solves problems by being very observant of small details. With her help, the group was able to defeat many Sagakos more effectively.

However, Yuko's power weakens over time, and she reaches a point where she seals herself in an onion along with another Sagako as a sacrificial act.

The last to join is Eikichi Hyodo, Yuko's brother, who joins against his will when his sister turns into an onion and is forced to fight the Sagakos because he also has the power to seal these curses. Along with Tae's training, Eikichi dedicated himself to fighting and learning with the Sagako Busters to defeat the curse and get his sister back.

However, the curse grows stronger every day, generating more and more Sagakos, so the Busters must find new ways to fight this threat. During his participation in the group, Eikichi slowly shows himself to be just as effective as his sister with Sagako's seals.

The Busters' most difficult challenge was fighting the spider Sagako, which turned out to be none other than the girl that Tae's parents found and raised. Magatsuhi splits up the group by kidnapping Anna and Hanako, leaving Tae and Eikichi on their own. The group meets again at the Takeo Ureshino Marchen Mura Village Amusement Park, where Tae and Eikichi are kidnapped by Magatsuhi and discover that the onions Eikichi put a blanket on have hatched and the Sagako inside have been released. Thanks to the purified Sagako, they fight Magatsuhi with all of their might.

Tae, who was already wounded from the battle, makes the ultimate sacrifice by using the Misogi power of the onions to seal Magatsuhi within her body. Wiping out the Sagako and the power of the onions in the process. Yuko is freed from her onion, now with the antlers of the Sagako she fused with, and realizes that her twin brother is now bigger than her. Hanako then cuts off her antlers with an electric saw.

By 1994, the Sagako Busters girls have moved on with their lives; Yuko gets married and is now a mother, Hanako now does scientific research, and Anna became a police officer and reconciled with her family. Jofuku has rejuvenated and opened a new adult store. The group gathers on the fifth anniversary of Tae's death for their “promised day” at the cemetery where her grave is.

Although she seems somewhat conceited by her attitude, actually from her perspective she wants to help Ai Mizuno get out of the old-fashioned prefecture of Saga and manage to become a great idol with Iron Frill. But the way she expresses her offer is quite selfish by belittling Franchouchou and telling them that they are nothing compared to her group. Despite this, she shows to have admiration for Ai and wants to overcome what she did to her in her life without having to go through the same fate as her.

Later, it is shown that her attitude towards Ai is because she admired her since she was a little girl and dreamed of being like Ai. This is highlighted by Yui, who tells her to leave the past behind and focus on what is coming.
ADVERTISEMENT

Etymology

The name Shiori means “poem” (詩) (shi) and “weave, weaving” (織) (ori).
Shiori's surname Baba means “horse” (馬) (ba) and “field, place” (場) (ba).
Trivia

Shiori seems like she had admiration for Ai Mizuno in her lifetime and now wants to get over her.
Shiori would be the equivalent of Sakura Minamoto if she hadn't been run over and killed by a truck.
This is confirmed in episode 16 as Shiori had admired Ai since she was about 7–8 years old, which explains her attitude to include her in Iron Frill.
Shiori's voice actors have both done voice work for other idol anime characters:
Her Japanese voice actress voiced Nico Yazawa in Love Live! School Idol Project.
Her English voice actress voiced Chika Takami in Love Live! Sunshine!!

Ito seems to be already in his adulthood and knows how to defend himself very well when Yugiri attacked him, so it appears that he received some kind of training. He wears a blue Yukata throughout the episode and classic wooden shoes from the Meiji era. His physical appearance makes him look quite young. His hair is gray as well as his eyes, and he always seems to wear a serious appearance when he is not with Kiichi Momozaki.
Personality

Ito is Kiichi's friend, shown during Yugiri's past in the second season. Two years prior, he caught his attention since he heard of a madman in Saga trying to recover the old prefecture.

He went to make fun of him, but he ended up feeling sorry for that nobody was paying attention to him. He is always following Kiichi wherever he goes and from time to time they go out to eat or to the park; however, he constantly tries to make Kiichi forget his plan to save Saga for some reason and tells him that he should become a doctor and study because he is very intelligent.

Ito is shown as someone serious and with charisma who does not want to repeat the war of 1874 and recommends to Kiichi that if he continues like this, he will create a new uproar in Saga. Ito is serious when he realizes that Yugiri is helping him with his plan, and they are getting people from Saga to join the cause.

He is the only one who seems to tolerate Kiichi, joking with him and fulfilling his dream of restoring Saga. But for a while, it is unknown how genuine this is since he is in Saga to eliminate the insurgents. He would eventually almost kill Kiichi if it weren't for Yugiri's intervention. However, when he dies, it is clear that he did, after all, see something in Kiichi's dream, and dies regretfully that he betrayed his friend.

Despite assassinating several of the rebels and almost killing Kiichi, deeply Ito always wanted to see him fulfill his objective of saving Saga. But unfortunately for him, his work forced him to avoid new revolts. In the end, Ito was always noble with his actions and showed appreciation for the people he knew to the point of sacrificing himself for Kiichi to build a new Saga. The anime shows his actions as antagonistic towards Saga and Yugiri, but in reality, it was what shaped the prefecture that it is today and led to Yugiri's beheading before her resurrection a couple of centuries later.
ADVERTISEMENT

Skillset

Impersonification—Ito was able to mimic the police officer’s voice to scare Kiichi Momozaki into thinking he was in trouble again.
Swordsmanship—As seen in Episode 21, Ito is skilled with the katana to the point of taking down several men much larger than him and assassinating them in the process.
Encryption—The letter that Ito throws to the tramp at the end of the episode is encrypted and says the following:
If/when the target's supporters gather… I couldn't confirm the target until now. There is a high probability that they will spread from now on.
Etymology

The name Shojiro means “right, proper” (正) (sho), “next” (次) (ji) and “son” (郎) (ro).
Shojiro's surname Ito means “that one” (伊) (i) and “east” (東) (to).
ADVERTISEMENT

Trivia

Ito appears to be a member of the Kenpeitai, the secret police of the Japanese army. Considering they were founded in 1881, just two years before the events of Saga Jihen parts One and Two, it lines up with the timeline and would also explain why Ito was able to defend himself so quickly from Yugiri's chopsticks. He also mentions that he only became friends with Kiichi Momozaki after learning of his political views. With all of this, it doesn't bode well for Kiichi or Yugiri to have attracted his attention.
He is named after Kashitaro Ito, an officer of the Shinsengumi.[1]
Later it is confirmed that he was part of the government and was sent to Saga to avoid new revolts.
Despite murdering rebels and almost killing Kiichi and Yugiri, Ito was only doing his job to get ahead, and as his phrase “The country is corrupt and ruthless” shows some people are forced to do questionable jobs to continue with their life.
His full name is known only in the credits; he is addressed solely by his last name on the show itself.
The group picture of him, Ito, and Yugiri can be seen resting on one of the shelves in the Jofuku Bar near the end of “Episode 21”.
He has many moments that frame him in a rather sinister tone.
Yugiri nearly incapacitates him when he enters her house uninvited. He has nothing but a stern look on his face as he blocks her blow with a fan.
At the end of his debut, he is seen passing a note to an informant on the streets.
He is eventually revealed to be a government agent sent to subdue any attempted armed rebellion. He does it by killing a group of rebellious samurai

Skull and Bull[1] (デスおじ, Desu Oji) are a pair of major supporting characters and are two of Franchouchou's first-ever fans. After the girls' performance in the first episode, they are continuously seen in the audience for all their future performances.

Appearance

Skull

He wears a black leather jacket and underneath a purple shirt, pants are made of torn black leather, and he wears black boots too. He has a short black and purple striped skirt. In terms of physical appearance, he is quite skinny, and his face is thin and pale. He wears his neck-length gray hair as part of his hairstyle.

Despite the fact that he is lanky, he shows great physical ability and flexibility when it comes to fighting.

Bull

He has a red shirt that does not fit well with his physique, so he constantly shows his belly. He has a black skirt with pink stripes over gray pants and black boots, just like the other metalhead. When it comes to physical appearance, he is quite fat and chubby. On his cheeks, he has a red star tattooed on a yellow ray. His hair is brown and has the shape of a drop, in addition to wearing ray decorations on it.

Personalities

As they are complete outsiders to the idol fandom. They were at first they are confused and irritated when their announced metal concert turns out to be a front for an idol group, only to quickly come to love the girls and their work throughout the series.

They have stayed with Franchouchou since the first and somewhat disastrous performance at Geils. Even by the time, the girls hit rock bottom in Revenge, these two still refuse to give them up. Taken to another level in the first episode of Revenge, where they team up with Kotaro to animate an encore by Franchouchou, despite the angry crowd that was already beginning to assault Kotaro for his tireless cheers. Even going so far as to fight alongside Kotaro as they outnumbered just so Franchouchou could perform their song without being booed off the stage.

Bull is noted to be somewhat of a masochist, as when he sees Saki kicking Takeo, he says that this is why Number 2 is the best in his opinion and states that it must be nice for her to kick him while blushing.
Trivia

In the English dub, Skull speaks with a Birmingham accent.
The only time the two were not shown together was in “Episode 6” where only Metalhead B is seen taking selfies with the girls in the crowd with Metalhead A nowhere to be found.
The only episodes wherein they don’t make appearances during Franchouchou’s performances those days were in “Episode 3” and “Episode 4”.
Granted, they were only absent in the third episode, since it being a guerrilla performance meant they had no idea of the event and location.
It is revealed in the spin-off manga, Zombie Land Saga Gaiden: The First Zombie, the two are former classmates of Eikichi Hyodo.
Funimation's dubbing for season two calls them “Skull and Bull” a reference to the first comedic duo of the show Mighty Morphin' Power Rangers, Bulk and Skull.
Death Metal Fan A's social media is really called Death Metal Fan A as Chapter 28 of the manga confirmed.

Takeo is a huge, burly man with very small eyes. He has a noticeable self-inflicted scar on his left eye, caused scratching his face in a moment of anger and sadness from the loss of Lily.

When working, he dons a baby blue high collar utility shirt with a towel on his neckline and/or a hard hat. His facial hair is unshaven and eyebrows are unkempt. Outside of work, he dons a gray vest with a white-collar shirt and a blue tie, while having no facial hair and neat eyebrows.

Teens

Takeo's appearance in 1989 is very different from what he is today. It was revealed that he used to be a school delinquent and have dyed hair along with pompadour and was not yet bald.

Personality

Present

Despite his gigantic size and intimidating appearance, Takeo is a genuinely kind and friendly guy to others, and generally a quiet and reserved man. He makes this noticeable at the Franchouchou concert in Episode 8; he remembers the time with Lily Hoshikawa and finally manages to put it behind him.

He seems to deeply regret how his last words to Lily were derogatory about the fact that Lily was distressed about growing body hair, due to her not wanting to go through puberty. He cries hard after Lily's death, clearly blaming himself for overworking her.

Teens

Takeo alias “Big Foot” was the strongest student of his school and of the time. For that very reason, a gang called Q-taro decided to recruit him for his strength. The objective of this gang was to conquer the country and be the kings of the gangs of the time. However, Takeo was only looking for something more powerful, “love”.

Despite being big and generating fear in people, he is someone with a big heart and shows a lot of affection for people who appreciate him as he really is. Although he has incidents when he tries to confess his love, he keeps trying until he succeeds. Sachika, his future wife, accepts his proposal to marry him in the future.

Takeo's surname Go means “overpowering, great, powerful, excelling, Australia, fine feathers, writing brush, little” (豪).
Trivia

When Takeo is asked about how the crew came up with his character design, they responded how they “wanted to draw ugly men for a change” which would make others question if Takeo himself is whether or not a human being.[1]
As revealed by Lily Hoshikawa in Takeo’s debut episode, he wears size 5XL clothes.
Takeo shares the same name as one of the cities located within the Saga Prefecture.
He received a head kick from 105lb (ca. 48 kg) Saki that somehow had enough power to knock him over and instantly knock him out.
According to Lily, he sang the song “Life” because his wife loved it in life.
He is one of the characters that appear in the prequel manga Zombie Land Saga Gaiden: The First Zombie. He studied at Saga Minami High School. Which years later Maimai Yuzuriha would attend.
During his stay at school, he was mistaken for a Sagako due to his large size.
During Chapter 6, he has trouble confessing to Sachika because of a Sagako who avoids him every time he tries. But, he didn't give up due to his bad luck and thanks to the Saga Sagako Busters he manages to declare his love for her.
When he was born, his parents mistook him for a demon because of his large size and large face; hence his parents called him Takeo, in honor of his large size.
Despite being acquainted with Tae Yamada, he did not seem to recognize her during his first meeting with Franchouchou, despite noting the similarities between “Number 6” and his late daughter.
