White Ryu (ホワイト竜, Howaitoryū) is Saki Nikaido’s childhood idol who inspired her to become the person she is today from when she was in middle school. He is a minor character who made his debut in “The SAGA of an Almost-Broken Radio”.

Appearance

Young

A fairly athletic man in his 35s. He has peculiar long hair and a retro look that stands out from the rest of the artists; his pompadour is extremely long and stocky.

Present

Regardless of the era, White Ryu proudly sports a hairstyle with a pompadour and sunglasses. His hairstyle, straight in the 90s, falls on his face, he has to push it with his hand to show his face. With age, his hair changes from dark brown to a grayish color. In 2019, White Ryu is older than he was at the beginning of his career and his face is slightly wrinkled, Lily finds White Ryu's appearance cheesy while Saki discovers that he hasn't changed almost anything since the 90s.

Personality

Although at first glance he seems the typical conceited artist who thinks of himself, he is a good guy who continues to maintain his style from when he was mostly seen and constantly tries to give a message to people about finding their way and making others shine. Although his advice is out of date, he always tries to strive to find the path that leads to the truth and likes to guide and inspire others. In his debut episode, he shows his cool personality by leaving Saki his legacy of continuing on the radio because he knows that Saga needs new energy.
Etymology

White Ryu and Hakuryu literally translate to “White Dragon”, Ryu means dragon in Japanese, and Haku means white.
Trivia

His appearance and demeanor are in many ways based on satire of the Japanese youth motorcycle gangs “Bosozoku”, which were popular from the 70s to the 90s and to which female part Saki and Reiko belonged to.
White Ryu's character is inspired by the real Japanese singer and actor Hakuryu. The latter interprets the character and the song “Do You Hate Windy Days?”. He also participated in the first announcement trailer for Zombie Land Saga Revenge, in July 2019, where he plays a mysterious character who wishes to take revenge.
Hakuryu is quite known for his Yakuza movies and his collection of sunglasses.
Hakuryu is from Imari, a city located in Saga Prefecture.
In Episode 24, Ryu is seen arriving in Saga with the US military, but they carry a blue US flag, indicating that they came from international aid.
For the origin of the character White Ryu, it was decided that he would not be an ordinary person, but someone who would turn out to be cool and passionate. A person who anyone would think is rare at first glance. Perfect qualities for Saki, who, like her, doesn't care what others say.

Yuko Hyodo (兵動 裕子, Hyōdō Yūko) is Eikichi's sister and the top beauty of the high school. She is in charge of purifying Sagako's curse. As a result of being fatally injured in a battle with a Sagako, she had to be substituted by her brother as a member of the Sagako Busters.

She is a character introduced in the Zombie Land Saga Gaiden: The First Zombie spin-off manga.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


00:00

41:20

Yuko is a high school girl, so she wears a high school outfit consisting of a knee-length light blue skirt and a dark blue jacket with a collared shirt underneath. Her hair and eyes are golden, and her hair is quite long and straight.

In terms of her physical appearance, Yuko is quite a weak girl in combat. When she is dressed as Sagako Buster, she wears a white uniform and some additional accessories. Her height was the same as her twin brother, Eikichi, before merging with Sagako. Already fused, she reveals huge antlers of the Sagako Niji-no matsubara, which are then cut with an electric saw.
Personality

Yuko is a pretty good girl, even winning awards at her school for attendance and having the highest grades. Unlike her brother, who was mediocre at everything, she was the ideal girl both in her school and on the farm.

She tried to protect Saga from the curses and also her brother's life at all costs, even giving her life in exchange for it. She has something altruistic about the selfless actions she takes in trying to protect her and Saga's brother's daily lives at the expense of her own.

Being familiar with the Sagako, she can more easily understand their motives and their emotions at the time of being sealed. Even sealed, she lovingly treats the onions with Sagako inside so that one day her feelings will pass to them, and it will be possible to communicate with Sagako.

When she met Tae, she promised that she would not let any Sagako harm people. Even when she was a child, she showed her bravery by defending Tae from a Sagako. Thanks to this, the two started working together at Karatsu Burger when the place was about to close due to low sales, bringing prosperity and fame to the place. Tae, who only had revenge and grudge in her heart, sees in Yuko the feelings she never thought she felt, which inevitably made her become attached to Yuko.

As the good sister that she is, she cares a lot for her older brother and always encourages him to keep going even though he usually puts himself down. She knows that he has potential and will continually try to help her brother achieve his goals. After being freed from the onion, she reveals that she has seen and heard all the struggles her brother had throughout his journey in Sagako Busters Saga, being grateful and proud of her older brother.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Skillset

Harvesting—In the day, Yuko was a farmer on her family farm, and she was responsible for the harvests of the onions that grew on them to sell them. Some onions she also kept as a charm.
Enhanced Intelligence—Being the opposite of her brother, she was highly intelligent in school and popular with her class, which subsequently earned her several accolades.
Unique Abilities

Exorcism—She had a unique ability to permanently exorcise the Sagakos thanks to the use of onions grown on her farm. The Hyodo twins have access to this ability, being able to seal Sagako using the onions from their farm. Yuko specialized in this during her time as Sagako Buster.
Etymology

The name Yuko means “abundant” (裕) (yu) and “child” (子) (ko).
Yuko's surname Hyodo means “soldier, warrior” (兵) (hyo) and “dynamic, motion, change, confusion” (動) (do).

Trivia

Tae Yamada says that Yuko does the purification ritual for miko (巫女 の 禊). The reason Tae thinks it's ridiculous for a child to do it is that miko (shrine maidens) are traditionally young maidens. It's part of the Shinto tradition, and the overall story is infused with Shinto vibes. In literature, manga, and anime, miko are often portrayed as heroines who fight evil spirits, demons, and ghosts.
Junko Konno is revealed to be the idol of Yuko Hyodo and the reason why the latter wanted to become idols alongside Tae, as revealed in the thirteenth chapter of the spin-off manga.
She, alongside Tae, are the only humans to have been fused with Sagako.
In her case, she was unintentionally fused with the Niji-no matsubara Sagako after she sealed it away in an onion whilst sacrificing her own body. After being freed from the onion, it is revealed that she absorbed the Sagako's antlers.
It is revealed in the last chapter that she is now married and has a daughter, possibly a cast member of the anime.

The Saga Prefecture (佐賀県, Saga-ken) is located on the north side of Kyushu Island, Japan. The prefecture is the main setting for the events of the Zombie Land Saga anime series.

Description (Real Life)

History

In ancient times, the area composed of Nagasaki Prefecture and Saga Prefecture was called Hizen Province. The current name dates from the Meiji Restoration. Rice farming culture has prospered here since ancient times, and vestiges can be seen at the ruins of Nabatake in Karatsu and the Yoshinogari site in Yoshinogari.

Feudal Period

From the Kamakura period to the Muromachi period, it is thought that over 100 feudal clans existed. Also exerting great influence during this time was a samurai clan operating along the Genkai Sea called the Matsuratō. Upon entering the Sengoku period, the Ryūzōji clan expanded their control to include all of the Hizen and Chikugo Provinces, and part of the Higo and Chikuzen Provinces. After the death of daimyō Takanobu Ryūzōji, Naoshige Nabeshima took control of the political situation, and by 1607 all of the Ryūzōji clan's domain was under the control of the Nabeshima clan.

In the Edo period, this area was called the Saga Domain, and it included three sub-domains: the Hasunoike, Ogi, and Kashima Domains. Also within the current borders of Saga Prefecture during this time were the Karatsu Domain and two territories of the Tsushima-Fuchū Domain. Saga Domain and its sub-domains continued to be ruled by the Nabeshima clan, its various illegitimate family lineages, and members of the former Ryūzōji clan. Politically, the area was relatively stable. However, the cost of defending Nagasaki was increasing and difficult from the start. The financial situation was worsened by the great Kyōhō famine and the Siebold Typhoon of 1828. Nevertheless, due to the large area of reclaimed land from the Ariake Sea arable land was able to increase significantly and by the 1840s the annual koku of Saga Domain increased to about 670,000, twice that of 200 years before.

Around the middle of the 19th century, Naomasa Nabeshima strove to set right the domain's financial affairs, reduce the number of government officials, and encourage local industries such as Arita porcelain, green tea, and coal. Also, thanks to the proximity of the international port of Nagasaki, new technologies were introduced from overseas, such as the reverberatory furnace and models of steam locomotives.

After the Boshin War, many people from Saga Domain assisted in the Meiji Restoration. In the Meiji era the modernization of coal mines in Kishima and Higashimatsuura districts, among others, progressed, bolstered by the construction of railroads.

Geography

Kyushu's prefecture, Saga, is located on the northwest corner of the island, bordered by the Genkai Sea and the Tsushima Strait to the north and the Ariake Sea to the south. Saga's proximity to mainland Asia has made it an important gateway for the transmission of culture and trade throughout Japanese history. Largely rural outside of the two largest cities of Saga and Karatsu, agricultural and forested lands comprise over 68% of the total prefectural land area. There are six prefectural parks and one quasi-national park in Saga.

1870-1883

During the Bakumatsu, the Saga prefecture was Westernized faster than other places in Japan, so it was a key place during the reform. But after the samurai revolts in 1874 and the defeats of the wars, its glory remained in the past. By 1876 Saga Prefecture had been divided between Mizuma and Nagasaki, which completely erased it from the map. [1]

After the war, Kiichi Momozaki was orphaned and taken in by Jofuku to restore Saga Prefecture in later years. After 10 years of attempts, Yugiri arrives in Saga and meets Kiichi in the city park. With Yugiri's help, he speaks out to take back Saga Prefecture, which attracts Saga's former ruling class, who want to take back the prefecture in a non-peaceful way. This triggers a revolt in the prefecture, which leads to its rising from the ashes In 1883.[2]

1989-1999

Saga succumbs to the plague of curses called Sagako, which are a manifestation of Saga's curse that wants to prevent Saga from prospering and being successful. However, a group of brave warriors are willing to fight against this scourge, giving their lives in exchange for Saga's sake. The Saga Sagako Busters are the group in charge of dealing with the manifestations of the curse, and with the help of Jofuku, They are responsible for preventing the curse from taking people's lives and making Saga prosperous.

2018-2020

During this time, Saga suffers from constant depopulation and threatens to become depopulated. Kotaro Tatsumi gathers a group of zombie girls to bring back attention to Saga being a group of successful idols, causing Saga to have something that people cannot forget.

After the severe flooding in the prefecture in 2020, Franchouchou, with the help of Kotaro's promotion and Ookoba, make everyone turn their eyes to Saga and the disaster that befell. This not only helps revive the prefecture, but also helps those dignified by the floods. [3]

Unknown.

The Curse of SAGA

The curse takes different forms over time. For example, during the Meiji era, the curse manifested itself by tricking people into leading to war and destruction. At the end of the eighties, when there was a period of relative normality, the curse was embodied by Sagako, curses with physical forms that terrified the inhabitants of Saga. Currently, the curse appears as natural disasters and/or strange accidents that point to Franchouchou's ascension.

Franchouchou itself was created by Kotaro Tatsumi as part of his Zombie Land Saga project, designed and ultimately to defeat the curse and thus save Saga. Because the curse promises to kill any individual who can bring glory to Saga, the project is Kotaro's attempt to circumvent its power by producing an idol group made up entirely of undead zombies.

Now, that the curse realizes it can't kill the dead, it targets the only living member. The curse already tried to kill Kotaro by attacking him near the sea and through the huge object that fell into the EFS, but in both circumstances, Kotaro survived. Now death will target the Saga itself, creating the Sagapocalypse. In episode 13, Kotaro said, “Is this hell?” which can be interpreted as “Is this the curse that is trying to stop us?”

In the last two episodes, Kotaro will desperately attempt to keep the saga together so that the girls can finally save Saga at the EFS concert.

Trivia

The anime's title, Zombie Land Saga, refers both to the saga (story) of the idol pop group made up of zombies and to the prefecture itself.
As such, each episode has the word “Saga” included somewhere in the title.
In real life, Jofuku did come to Saga and found the elixir of immortality in one of the mountains of the prefecture, which caused the wrath of a Chinese demigod.
During Franchouchou's concert “Zombie Land Saga LIVE ~Franchouchou Saga, come with me~!” donations were opened to help with repairs after the floods in August 2020, raising 1.8 million yen (US $16,000) [4]
The Saga Prefecture emblem is pretty similar to the emblem of the fictional SCP foundation. Some users theorize that the Saga Prefecture government is some kind of organization that is aware of supernatural activity in the prefecture. However, in real life, this is nothing more than a coincidence.
It is revealed in the spin-off manga that if a Sagako were to be taken outside of the prefecture's borders, it will explode, resulting to its demise.
Similarly, this is also hinted to be the case for Zombies in Kotaro Tatsumi's dialogue in “The Acoustic SAGA of Love and Youth” about rejecting work for Ai Mizuno that involves going outside of Saga.

Saga City (佐賀市, Saga-shi) is the capital city of Saga Prefecture, located on the island of Kyushu, Japan. Saga was the capital of the Saga domain in the Edo period and the largest city in the ancient province of Hizen.

In real life

Saga is located in the southeastern part of Saga Prefecture. After the 2005 merger, the city became very long from north to south, skirting the Ariake Sea to the south and Fukuoka prefecture to the southeast and north. The northern half of the city contains the Sefuri Mountains. Saga can also be considered within the Greater Fukuoka metropolitan area and, by extension, the Fukuoka-Kitakyushu metropolitan area.

On April 1, 1889, the modern municipal system was established and the city of Saga was founded. At the same time, the current region of the city is occupied by 21 villages from three districts.

On October 1, 2007, the cities of Higashiyoka, Kawasoe, and Kubota (all of the Saga district) were incorporated into Saga. (population: approximately 240,000; area: 431.42 km2) The Saga district was dissolved as a result of this merger.

In the series

The city of Saga is one of the main cities where anime events are held, especially the GEILS death metal concerts of Franchouchou, or for its part, most of the main events of the series together with the city of Karatsu. Also, here is the New Jofuku bar that Kotaro frequently visits when he has doubts about the Zombie Land Saga Project.
